coach.name: Rooky
coach.blurb: Your coach. Rooky explains every move, cheers your best ones and helps you learn from the rest.

opponents.name: Truffle
opponents.blurb: Brand new to chess. Truffle hops about happily and often leaves pieces where you can take them.
opponents.hello: Hi! I'm Truffle. I only just learned how the pieces move. Let's have fun!
opponents.win: Hooray for you! You won! Can we play again?
opponents.lose: I won? I won! Thank you for playing with me!
opponents.draw: A draw! We both did great.

opponents.name: Bramble
opponents.blurb: A calm builder. Bramble brings out the pieces one by one and avoids tricks.
opponents.hello: Hello, I'm Bramble. I like to build my position one piece at a time.
opponents.win: Well built! You knocked my dam right down.
opponents.lose: My dam held this time. Keep building, you're getting stronger!
opponents.draw: Nobody broke through. A sturdy draw!

opponents.name: Zippy
opponents.blurb: Races into attack! Zippy is fast, sometimes a little too fast.
opponents.win: Whoa, you were faster than me! Great game!
opponents.lose: Zoom! Got you this time. Watch out for my quick attacks!
opponents.draw: Phew! All that rushing, and it's a draw!

opponents.name: Shelly
opponents.blurb: Slow and steady. Shelly defends well and loves a long endgame.
opponents.hello: Good day. I'm Shelly. I take my time, and I never give up.
opponents.win: Well done. Slow and steady, but you were steadier!
opponents.lose: Slow and steady wins the race. Try again, and take your time!
opponents.draw: A long, patient draw. My favourite kind of game.

opponents.name: Rocco
opponents.blurb: A sneaky trickster who sets traps. Look twice before you grab a piece!
opponents.hello: Psst! I'm Rocco. I have a few tricks up my sleeve. Can you spot them?
opponents.win: You saw through all my tricks! Very impressive.
opponents.lose: Ha! You fell into one of my traps. Look twice next time!
opponents.draw: Hmm, a draw. You're hard to trick!

opponents.name: Ivy
opponents.blurb: Sees far across the board and makes patient plans.
opponents.hello: Hello from up here! I'm Ivy, and I can see the whole board.
opponents.win: Splendid! You saw even further than I did.
opponents.lose: From up here I spotted a plan. You'll see it next time!
opponents.draw: We both saw everything. A well-earned draw.

opponents.name: Onyx
opponents.blurb: Sharp and clever. Onyx calculates deeply and loves a surprise sacrifice.
opponents.hello: Caw! I'm Onyx. I calculate every move. Do you?
opponents.lose: Caw! I saw that combination coming. Keep sharpening your tactics!
opponents.draw: A draw. You calculated very well.

opponents.name: Ember
opponents.blurb: Full strength. Ember thinks the longest and plays the very best moves.
opponents.hello: So, you dare to face Ember the Dragon? Let us play!
opponents.win: Incredible! You have tamed the dragon. You are a true champion!
opponents.lose: Roar! Even champions lose to dragons. Try again!
opponents.draw: A draw against a dragon is a mighty result!

coach.name: Miu
coach.hello: You have learned well. Now play me! Win, and the Pharaoh's Treasure set is yours.
coach.win: Purr-fect! The Pharaoh's Treasure belongs to you now.
coach.lose: So close! Every great player loses on the way. Try again!

stages.title: Games of the pharaohs
pages: Welcome to Egypt, more than 3,000 years ago! The great river Nile flows past temples and pyramids, and in the palace the young pharaoh Tutankhamun is playing a board game called Senet.
Chess had not been invented yet. It would appear in India about two thousand years later. But the Egyptians loved games of skill, and Tutankhamun was buried with several Senet boards.
I am Miu. Cats were treasured in ancient Egypt, you know. Today I will teach you the knight, the piece shaped like a horse. The pharaoh's horses pulled his golden chariots!

quiz.q: Which board game did Tutankhamun play?
quiz.explain: Senet is one of the oldest board games we know. Chess came much later.

stages.title: The chariot race
objectives: Catch treasure with an L-shaped jump

steps.say: The pharaoh's chariot horses are racing along the Nile! Your knight is a chariot horse: it leaps over anything in its way and lands two squares along and one to the side.

exercises.prompt: Rocks block the road. Click every square the knight on g2 can leap to.
hints: The pawns next to the knight do not stop it.
Near the edge of the board a knight has fewer jumps.

exercises.prompt: A golden scarab lies on d7. Jump onto it and take it.
hints: Two squares to the left, then one square up.

exercises.prompt: A black pawn is racing to become a queen. Catch it with your knight!
hints: The pawn is on b2.
One square down and two to the left.

stages.title: Tomb treasure
stages.intro: Treasure is lying about! In each puzzle, find a piece you can take for free.

coach.name: Sophie
coach.hello: Let us see if you are as wise as an owl. Win, and the Olympian Marble set is yours.
coach.win: Wonderful! Athena herself would be proud of you.
coach.lose: Even the wisest owl loses sometimes. Think, then try again.

stages.title: Thinkers and their games
pages: Welcome to Athens! On the hill called the Acropolis, builders are finishing the Parthenon, a temple of white marble for the goddess Athena.
The Greeks played a game called petteia, trapping the other side's pieces on a grid. The philosopher Plato wrote about it! Greek thinkers loved numbers and logic, just like chess players.
I am Sophie. The owl was Athena's bird, a sign of wisdom. Wise players count before they capture: a pawn is worth 1, a knight or a bishop 3, a rook 5 and a queen 9.

quiz.q: How many points is a rook worth?
quiz.explain: A rook is worth 5: more than a knight or a bishop, less than a queen.

stages.title: The agora market
objectives: Add up the points on each side

steps.say: In the market of Athens, traders count every coin. Chess players count too! Before you take a piece, add up what you win and what you might lose.

exercises.prompt: Which is worth more: two knights, or one rook?
options: They are worth exactly the same
exercises.explain: Two knights add up to 6 points, one more than a rook.

exercises.prompt: Two black pieces are left unguarded. Take the more valuable one with your queen.
hints: A bishop is worth 3 and a rook is worth 5.
Your queen can reach a4 along the diagonal.

exercises.prompt: Should your rook take the knight on e5?
options: No: the pawn on d6 takes back, and you give 5 points for 3
exercises.explain: The knight is guarded by the d6 pawn, so you would swap your rook (5) for a knight (3).

stages.title: The owl's eyes
stages.intro: An owl sees everything. Count what each side can take, then win the most valuable piece.

coach.name: Marcus
coach.hello: Ave! Show me the courage of a Roman. Win, and the Imperial Rome set is yours.
coach.win: Victory! You fight like a true Roman.
coach.lose: Rome was not built in a day. Try again!

stages.title: The game of little soldiers
pages: Welcome to Rome! Emperor Trajan has just finished a great column, carved with a spiral of more than 2,500 figures that winds all the way to the top.
Roman soldiers played ludus latrunculorum, the game of little soldiers. You captured an enemy piece by trapping it between two of your own.
I am Marcus. In Rome's oldest legend, a wolf looked after the twins Romulus and Remus. A battle is won when the enemy leader is trapped. In chess we call that checkmate!

options: The king is attacked and cannot escape
quiz.explain: Checkmate ends the game: the king is in check and has no way out.

stages.title: The legion's wall
objectives: Mate with a wall of rooks

steps.say: Roman soldiers locked their shields together to make a wall. Two rooks can do the same: one rook holds a whole row while the other gives check.

exercises.prompt: Black is to move. Is the black king checkmated?
options: Yes: it is in check and has no safe square
No: it can step to g8
No: it is not even in check
exercises.explain: The rook guards the whole back row and the king's own pawns block its way out.

exercises.prompt: Close the wall: checkmate in one move with your rooks.
hints: The rook on a7 already guards the seventh row.
Give check on the eighth row.

exercises.prompt: Your king helps your rook. Checkmate in one move.
hints: Your king guards a7 and b7.
Give check along the back row.

stages.title: Trap the general
stages.intro: Each puzzle has a checkmate in one move. Find it!

coach.name: Moti
coach.hello: Welcome to the emperor's court. Win, and the Maharaja's Jade set is yours.
coach.win: Shabash! Well played. The jade set is yours.
coach.lose: Elephants never forget, so remember this game and try again.

stages.title: Chaturanga
pages: Welcome to Agra! Emperor Shah Jahan is building the Taj Mahal, a tomb of white marble so beautiful that people still travel from all over the world to see it.

Chess was born in India about 1,500 years ago. It was called chaturanga, the four parts of an army: foot soldiers, horses, elephants and chariots. Today they are our pawns, knights, bishops and rooks.
I am Moti. Yes, the bishop used to be an elephant! Like elephants in a battle, chess pieces are strongest in the middle. Control the centre and your army can go anywhere.

quiz.explain: Chess began in India as chaturanga, then travelled to Persia, the Arab world and Europe.

stages.title: Elephants to the middle
objectives: Send your knights towards the middle

steps.say: In Akbar's palace the game began just like ours: pawns step into the middle and the pieces follow. A knight in the centre reaches eight squares. In the corner it reaches only two!

exercises.prompt: Which knight is stronger?
options: The knight on e4: it reaches 8 squares
The knight on h1: corners are safe
exercises.explain: A knight on the rim is dim. In the middle it attacks the most squares.

exercises.prompt: Bring your knight towards the centre.

wrong.g1h3: On h3 the knight sits at the edge and reaches only a few squares.

hints: Pick the square that points to the middle.

exercises.prompt: Which first move claims the centre?
exercises.explain: The d-pawn and e-pawn stand right in front of the four centre squares.

stages.title: The elephant's fork
stages.intro: Find a move that attacks two pieces at once. Your opponent can only save one!

coach.name: Bao
coach.hello: Ni hao! Patience and sharp eyes win games. Beat me, and the Ming Porcelain set is yours.
coach.win: Excellent! The porcelain set is yours. Handle it with care!
coach.lose: Bamboo grows slowly, but it grows strong. Try again!

stages.title: Elephants, cannons and a river
pages: Welcome to Beijing! The Forbidden City has just been finished: a palace of red walls and golden roofs with hundreds of buildings, where the emperor lived.
In China people play xiangqi, a cousin of chess. The pieces are flat discs with characters on them, a river runs across the middle of the board, and cannons jump over pieces to capture!
I am Bao. Pandas are patient, and patient players spot skewers: attack a big piece, and when it moves away, take the piece behind it.

quiz.q: What runs across the middle of a xiangqi board?
quiz.explain: The river divides the two armies. Some pieces move differently once they cross it.

stages.title: Bao's bamboo spear
objectives: Skewer a king with a bishop
Skewer a king with a rook

steps.say: A spear goes through the first target and reaches the one behind it. In a skewer you check the king, it must step away, and you take the piece standing behind it.

exercises.prompt: Give check with your bishop so the queen behind the king falls.
hints: The king and the queen stand on one diagonal.
Check from the long diagonal.

exercises.prompt: Now use your rook: check the king and win the rook behind it.
hints: The king and the black rook share a file.

exercises.prompt: In a skewer, which piece stands in front?
options: The more valuable piece, which must move away
exercises.explain: The big piece in front has to move, and the piece behind it is lost.

stages.title: The panda's skewer
stages.intro: Attack a valuable piece so that the piece behind it falls when it moves.

coach.name: Marco
coach.hello: Benvenuto! Let us see what you can do with a queen. Win, and the Murano Glass set is yours.
coach.win: Bravissimo! The Murano Glass set is yours.
coach.lose: So close! In Venice we say: little by little, one goes far. Try again!

stages.title: The queen gets her power
pages: Welcome to Venice, a city built on water, where people travel by gondola along the canals. On the island of Murano, glassmakers blow the finest glass in the world.

Long ago the queen could only move one square diagonally. Then, around 1475, players in Spain and Italy gave her new powers: she could move any distance, in any direction. People called it mad queen chess!
I am Marco. The winged lion is the symbol of Venice. With great power comes great care: bring your queen out too early and she will be chased all over the board.

quiz.q: What did the queen gain around 1475?
quiz.explain: That change made the queen the strongest piece and made chess much faster.

stages.title: The doge's warning
objectives: Punish a queen that comes out early

steps.say: In Venice the queen had just won her new powers, and players rushed her out. Here White's queen is out on move three, and Black's knight jumps out to attack her. Every chase gives you a free move.

exercises.prompt: Black's queen came out early. Bring out a piece that attacks her.
hints: A knight can attack the queen and develop at the same time.

exercises.prompt: You are Black. White's queen rushed out and attacks your e5 pawn. Guard it!

wrong.g8f6: The knight attacks the queen, but she takes e5 with check!

hints: The queen on h5 looks along the fifth row at e5.
A knight can guard e5 and come out at the same time.

exercises.prompt: Why should your queen wait a little at the start?
options: Smaller pieces can chase her and win time
She cannot move in the opening
exercises.explain: Bring out knights and bishops first. The queen joins once it is safe.

stages.title: Crown a new queen
stages.intro: Race your pawn to the far side and crown a brand-new queen before the black king catches it.

endgame.name: Crown a new queen
endgame.tip: Count the race! Only the two-square pawn jump outruns the black king. Then keep pushing.

coach.name: Gaston
coach.hello: Bonjour! In Paris every pawn dreams of becoming a queen. Win, and the Ruby & Pearl set is yours.
coach.win: Magnifique! The Ruby & Pearl set is yours.
coach.lose: Courage, my friend! Even the Eiffel Tower was built one piece at a time. Try again!

stages.title: The soul of chess
pages: Welcome to Paris in 1889! For the World's Fair, the city has built the tallest tower on Earth, made of iron lace. It is called the Eiffel Tower.
Not far away is the Café de la Régence, where people played chess for more than a hundred years. The great player Philidor learned the game there.
I am Gaston. The rooster is a symbol of France. Philidor said that pawns are the soul of chess. A pawn that nobody can stop may march all the way and become a queen!

quiz.q: What did Philidor call the pawns?
quiz.explain: Pawns decide the shape of the game, and a pawn that reaches the far side becomes a queen.

stages.title: Pawns on the march
objectives: Push a passed pawn to the far side

steps.say: At the Café de la Régence, Philidor watched his pawns like a general. A pawn with no enemy pawn in front of it, or on the files next to it, is a passed pawn. Nothing can block its march except pieces!

exercises.prompt: Which white pawn is a passed pawn?
exercises.explain: The black a-pawn guards the b-pawn's road and the black f-pawn guards the e-pawn's road. Nothing stands in the h-pawn's way.

exercises.prompt: The black king is far away. March your passed pawn!
hints: Count: the pawn needs three steps to reach a8.
Push the pawn, do not wait.

exercises.prompt: What happens when a pawn reaches the far side of the board?
options: It becomes a queen, or a rook, bishop or knight
It goes back to the start
It is taken off the board
exercises.explain: That is promotion. Most players choose a queen, the strongest piece.

stages.title: Café puzzles
stages.intro: The players at the café love a clever trick. Find the move that wins something.

coach.name: Mishka
coach.hello: Privet! Can you win an endgame against a bear? Win, and the Tsarina's Faberge set is yours.
coach.win: Molodets! Well done! The Faberge set is yours.
coach.lose: Bears are strong, but you are getting stronger. Try again!

stages.title: The endgame school
pages: Welcome to Saint Petersburg! Snow sparkles on golden domes, and the royal jewellers are making jewelled Easter eggs for the Tsar's family.
Russia loves chess. It has produced many world champions, and its chess schools are famous for teaching the endgame: the last part of the game, when only a few pieces are left.
I am Mishka. In the endgame even the king becomes a fighter! When two kings stand face to face with one square between them, we call it the opposition.

quiz.q: In the endgame, what should your king do?
quiz.explain: With fewer pieces about, the king is safe enough to help, and it is a strong piece.

steps.say: Two kings stand face to face in the snow, one square between them. Whoever does NOT have to move holds the opposition, and the other king has to give way.

exercises.prompt: Step in front of the black king and take the opposition.
hints: Leave exactly one square between the kings.

exercises.prompt: You are Black now. Take the opposition to block the white king.
hints: Face the white king on the same file.

exercises.prompt: The kings face each other with one square between. Who holds the opposition?
options: The side that does not have to move
The side that has to move
exercises.explain: Having to move is a problem here: your king must step aside.

stages.title: March of the pawn
stages.intro: Use a spare pawn move to win the opposition, then walk your pawn to the far side.

endgame.name: The spare pawn move
endgame.tip: Your king must not give way. Push the pawn one square to pass the move to Black, then march in front of your pawn.

coach.name: Skye
coach.hello: Welcome to the top of the world! This is the final challenge. Win, and the Manhattan Deco set is yours.
coach.win: Spectacular! You have travelled through time and won in every era.
coach.lose: Even eagles have to try again sometimes. You can do it!

stages.title: The city of chess clubs
pages: Welcome to New York in 1930! The Chrysler Building has just become the tallest building in the world, with a shining steel crown of arches and a needle-sharp spire.
The city is full of chess clubs, and the Manhattan Chess Club is one of the most famous in the world. The great Cuban champion José Raúl Capablanca played there.
I am Skye. From up high, an eagle sees the whole board. Strong players know their checkmate patterns by heart, so they can spot them in a flash.

quiz.q: Which world champion from Cuba played at the Manhattan Chess Club?
quiz.explain: Capablanca was world champion from 1921 to 1927 and was famous for his clear, simple style.

stages.title: Rooftop mates
objectives: Mate with king and queen together

steps.say: The famous New York clubs were full of players who knew their mates by heart. Here a king is smothered by its own pieces, and one knight jump finishes the game.

exercises.prompt: The king is boxed in by its own pieces. Checkmate in one.
hints: Only a knight can check this king.
Jump to f7.

exercises.prompt: Rook and knight team up. Checkmate in one.
hints: Your knight guards h7 and g8.
Bring the rook next to the king.

exercises.prompt: The queen needs her king's help. Checkmate in one.
hints: Your king guards g7.
Put the queen right next to the black king.

stages.title: Skyline finish
stages.intro: Each puzzle ends in checkmate. Find the moves that force it.
